name: Remote Access Hardware
summary: An adversary may use legitimate remote access hardware to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks. These services, including IP-based keyboard, video, or mouse (KVM) devices such as TinyPilot and PiKVM, are commonly used as legitimate tools and may be allowed by peripheral device policies within a target environment. strategies.name: Detect Remote Access via USB Hardware (TinyPilot, PiKVM)

analytics.name: Analytic 0446
analytics.guidance: Detection of USB-based remote access hardware (e.g., TinyPilot, PiKVM) attached to the host via drive or peripheral enumeration, triggering vendor identifiers or unusual EDID announcements.

analytics.name: Analytic 0447
analytics.guidance: Insertion of USB-based hardware proxies (e.g., PiKVM) which register under predictable names (e.g., tinypilot) or mount under known paths (e.g., /opt/tinypilot-privileged).

analytics.name: Analytic 0448
analytics.guidance: Attachment of hardware-backed USB KVM devices (e.g., TinyPilot) that enumerate new HID or serial communication interfaces with identifiable metadata.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: udev events or drive enumeration involving TinyPilot paths or device classes

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Hardware enumeration events via IOKit or USBMuxd showing TinyPilot or unknown keyboard/mouse
